findings.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — P1, confidence 100: `boolean userStorageCreated = user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential);` chooses the destination for the new set without deleting the recovery credential from the other destination, so when a provider starts or stops accepting this type between regenerations the credential manager continues validating the superseded local/external set and regeneration no longer invalidates every old code.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — P2, confidence 100: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` neither restricts validation to the requested next code nor removes a successful code, so every federated recovery-code login leaves the same code reusable and the next-code/exhaustion state permanently unchanged.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:86 — P2, confidence 100: `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId());` is also executed for models selected from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, so after an external provider validates its last code deletion is routed to Keycloak's stored-credential backend rather than that provider and the exhausted external credential remains configured.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:217 — P2, confidence 100: `public void disableCredentialType(RealmModel realm, UserModel user, String credentialType) { if (isOTPType(credentialType))` omits the newly supported recovery type, so an account/admin removal request for a federated recovery credential leaves that credential associated and configured in the external store.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:123 — P2, confidence 100: `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` reduces the typed recovery credential to an untyped code-list payload and discards its generated timestamp and user label, so every external implementation receives an incomplete record (as the changed stand-in demonstrates by substituting `Time.currentTimeMillis()` and a null label) and credential metadata drifts immediately on creation.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — P1, confidence 100: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` accepts every stored code without restricting validation to the requested next code or deleting a successful code, so entering code 12 when code 1 is requested or replaying any successful code authenticates repeatedly; the rebuttal that the form handles consumption fails because the form only reads the credential afterward and this provider never mutates `myUser.recoveryCodes`.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — P1, confidence 100: `boolean userStorageCreated = user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential);` enters a success branch that never deletes an existing local recovery credential, so a federated user who regenerates after gaining user-storage support retains pre-upgrade local codes that the credential-manager validation fallback still accepts; the rebuttal that `getCredential` prefers federated data fails because that preference governs rendering and exhaustion bookkeeping rather than the `isValid` provider chain.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:217 — P2, confidence 100: `if (isOTPType(credentialType))` and the matching `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` branch that adds only `CredentialModel.OTP` omit the new recovery-code sibling, so an account or admin removal request neither advertises nor clears `myUser.recoveryCodes`; the rebuttal that recovery metadata marks the type removable fails because federated removal is propagated through these `CredentialInputUpdater` methods.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:123 — P2, confidence 100: `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` forwards only the raw-code list and discards the generated-at timestamp and user label already present in `credentialModel`, so user-storage credentials lose the requested label and original creation metadata; the rebuttal that the storage provider can reconstruct them fails because neither value is present in the supplied `CredentialInput`.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — P1, confidence 100: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` accepts a stored recovery key without consuming it, so submitting the same generated key on two recovery logins authenticates both times and the user-storage path changes the existing one-time recovery-key intent into reusable backup passwords; the strongest rebuttal is that `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` handles consumption after validation, but its post-validation path only reads `allCodesUsed()` and never marks a federated code used, so that rebuttal fails.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:71 — P1, confidence 100: `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` can consume a valid one-time code and the new follow-up `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` at line 80 performs another unguarded user-storage read, so a provider failure between those calls returns a 500 after burning the code without completing login (and burns the user's last recovery path when it was the final code); the strongest rebuttal is that the request transaction rolls the validation back, but it fails because an external provider's independently committed consumption is outside Keycloak's transaction.

server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:57 — P2, confidence 100: `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst().or(() -> user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst())` lets any exception from the external provider escape before `.or(...)` can read the local fallback, so a transient provider outage turns recovery-form rendering and successful-login bookkeeping into a 500 even when a usable local credential exists; the strongest rebuttal is that providers should translate outages to an empty stream, but it fails because the SPI permits `getCredentials` to throw and `UserCredentialManager` directly returns that provider stream without containment.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — P2, confidence 100, advisory: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get())` and `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` at line 21 convert a missing or exhausted federated credential into `NoSuchElementException` and a 500, triggered whenever the earlier configured check races a concurrent deletion/last-code consumption or an eventually consistent provider returns stale state; the strongest rebuttal is that `configuredFor` guarantees both optionals are present, but it fails because configuration, credential enumeration, and code-list reads are separate non-atomic provider calls.

server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:57 — P2, confidence 75, advisory: the synchronous `getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst()` has no deadline or cancellation boundary, so when a user-storage provider blocks on its database/network every recovery challenge request occupies a server request thread indefinitely and retries amplify the exhaustion; the strongest rebuttal is that each provider should configure its own timeout, but it fails because the SPI imposes no timeout and this new authentication-path call invokes the provider directly.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:114 — P2 (confidence 100): adding `|| credentialType.equals(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` and the accompanying current-version recovery-code implementation rewrites a fixture whose own contract says it was “created in Keycloak 4.8.3” and future versions should work “without a need to change the code of this provider,” so when compatibility with an unchanged 4.8.3 provider regresses this suite now certifies a modernized provider instead; the strongest rebuttal is that this fixture conveniently supplies the user-storage behavior needed by the new test, but that does not preserve the compatibility claim because a separate contemporary test provider can exercise recovery keys without altering the historical baseline.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:72 — P1, confidence 100: `boolean isValid = authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` treats external `CredentialInputValidator.isValid` success as sufficient but never consumes the accepted code itself (the only subsequent deletion is gated on `allCodesUsed()`), so with the included provider’s unchanged predicate `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340`, replaying any previously accepted recovery code completes MFA indefinitely; the strongest rebuttal is that a provider can mutate its store inside `isValid`, but that generic validation contract does not require atomic one-time consumption and the provider shipped to demonstrate this new support performs no mutation, so the end-to-end supported path demonstrably violates recovery codes’ single-use security property.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:257 — P2, confidence 100: `testAppHelper.startLogin("otp1", "pass"); ... enterRecoveryCodes(enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage, driver, 0, recoveryKeys); ... enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage.clickSignInButton();` performs only one successful use and never replays that code, so the test stays green when the user-storage validator fails to consume recovery codes and the same code succeeds on a second login; the strongest rebuttal is that reaching `appPage` proves the authenticator path ran, but that proves first-use acceptance only and supplies no oracle for the required consumed-state transition.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:259 — P2, confidence 100: `enterRecoveryCodes(enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage, driver, 0, recoveryKeys);` supplies only a generated valid value, so the test remains green if the federated validator accepts arbitrary input or the configured flow bypasses rejection; the strongest rebuttal is that `appPage.assertCurrent()` confirms successful authentication, but a positive-only assertion cannot distinguish correct validation from unconditional acceptance.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:252 — P2, confidence 100: `assertUserDontHaveDBCredentials();` deliberately constrains the sole new scenario to the user-storage-success branch, so removing either the local creation fallback in `createRecoveryCodesCredential` or the local lookup fallback in `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` leaves this test green while providers that reject the recovery type can no longer use the existing database-backed path; the strongest rebuttal is that local recovery codes predate this change, but both local call sites were refactored here and this assertion prevents the changed test from exercising either fallback.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:197 — P3, confidence 75: `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse());` makes the test provider mirror the production helper's private choice to put an entire JSON code list in `challengeResponse`, and the same fixture later deserializes that field, so the browser test can pass without independently verifying the `CredentialInput` contract a real storage provider must consume; the strongest rebuttal is that the end-to-end login crosses the SPI boundary, but both sides of that boundary were changed together to share the same unasserted encoding assumption.

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the new createRecoveryCodesCredential method. Looking at the diff, when updateCredential returns true (userStorageCreated), the method logs success and returns. When it returns false, it creates the credential locally via recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(). However, there's no code to delete any existing credential from the other storage location before creating the new one. If a user previously had recovery codes in local storage and the user storage provider later starts accepting this credential type, updateCredential would succeed but the old local credential would remain. Similarly, if user storage stops accepting the type, the new credential goes to local storage but the old external credential remains. This means validation could succeed against superseded codes, which is a security/correctness bug.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the recovery code validation at line 340 uses `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` which only checks if the provided code exists in the list but does not: 1) verify it's the expected 'next' code in sequence, 2) remove or mark the code as used after successful validation. This means any valid recovery code can be reused indefinitely, which is a security bug for recovery codes that should be single-use. The RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel typically tracks which code is next and removes used codes, but this federated storage implementation bypasses that logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` first checks `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and falls back to local storage. When a federated credential is returned, the code in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (line 86, not shown in diff but referenced) calls `removeStoredCredentialById()` on the credential manager. This method targets Keycloak's local stored credentials, not the federated provider. So when the last recovery code from a federated credential is used, the deletion attempt goes to the wrong backend - the local storage instead of the external provider - leaving the exhausted external credential still configured.

Looking at the diff, the `isValid` method in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java` (lines 283-305) validates recovery codes by checking if the input matches any stored code via `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, but it never removes/consumes the used code from storage. adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural concern in the new getCredential() method added in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java. The code chains getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst().or(() -> getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst()). If getFederatedCredentialsStream() throws an exception from an external provider, the .or() fallback to local storage will never execute. adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:72 — P1, confidence 100: `boolean isValid = authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` treats external `CredentialInputValidator.isValid` success as sufficient but never consumes the accepted code itself (the only subsequent deletion is gated on `allCodesUsed()`), so with the included provider’s unchanged predicate `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340`, replaying any previously accepted recovery code completes MFA indefinitely; the strongest rebuttal is that a provider can mutate its store inside `isValid`, but that generic validation contract does not require atomic one-time consumption and the provider shipped to demonstrate this new support performs no mutation, so the end-to-end supported path demonstrably violates recovery codes’ single-use security property.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() at line 340 only checks if the code exists in the list (`return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`) but never removes/consumes the used code. The RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java at line 72 calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(credential)` and only deletes codes when `allCodesUsed()` returns true. This means the same recovery code can be replayed multiple times since the external storage provider's isValid doesn't consume the code, violating the single-use security property of recovery codes. adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:197 — P3, confidence 75: `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse());` makes the test provider mirror the production helper's private choice to put an entire JSON code list in `challengeResponse`, and the same fixture later deserializes that field, so the browser test can pass without independently verifying the `CredentialInput` contract a real storage provider must consume; the strongest rebuttal is that the end-to-end login crosses the SPI boundary, but both sides of that boundary were changed together to share the same unasserted encoding assumption.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a valid architectural concern: the test provider (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage) and the production code (CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential) both use the same JSON serialization approach for recovery codes via challengeResponse/credentialData. The test stores input.getChallengeResponse() directly as credentialData (line 197), while production serializes the codes list to JSON and passes it as challengeResponse (lines 117-123 in CredentialHelper). This creates a tight coupling where the test passes because both sides share the same encoding assumption, but there's no explicit contract verification. However, this is a test infrastructure concern rather than a bug - the end-to-end test does exercise the actual SPI boundary. It's a legitimate review point about test design but not a defect.
